prompt:
Add context-local translation callbacks throughout Click so applications can render different commands in different languages in the same Python process. Implement this as a maintained public feature across the command and parameter machinery, help formatting, parser errors, parameter types, exceptions, interactive terminal helpers, standard decorators and shell-completion diagnostics. Preserve the existing default output and supported Python versions.

Public API: Context accepts optional gettext and ngettext keyword arguments. Each is either None or callable; reject non-callable values with TypeError identifying the argument at construction. Context.gettext(message) calls the effective single-message callback. Context.ngettext(singular, plural, n) calls the effective plural callback, passing the original count. Each callback must return str; otherwise raise TypeError identifying gettext or ngettext. Empty strings and Unicode translations are valid. A None callback inherits that callback independently from the parent context; a root without one uses Python's existing gettext/ngettext behavior. The two methods work even when the Context is not on the current-context stack. Expose the callbacks through ordinary command context_settings and the existing context construction routes, with complete type annotations and API documentation.

Route Click-owned, user-facing messages that currently use gettext or ngettext through the applicable Context. Pass original message templates to the callback before interpolation, including plural templates and their real counts. Preserve placeholder names and existing interpolation semantics. Cover usage and help headings, automatic help/version option descriptions and version output, command/option/argument diagnostics, parameter conversion and range/choice/date/tuple errors, file/path errors, the standard exception wrappers and help hints, prompt validation and confirmation messages, pause/editor diagnostics, and shell-completion setup diagnostics. Deferred standard decorator messages must use the invocation's translation even when commands, options and types were constructed before the Context existed. Reusing the same command or type with different callbacks must not retain the first language. Caller-provided help, prompt labels, exception message text, version message templates, option names, choices and other values remain caller content; translate Click's surrounding standard templates without sending user content to the callback.

Use an explicit Context when the operation or exception has one, including direct type conversion and error formatting outside an active with block. Public helpers without an explicit Context use the current context when available and fall back to the existing gettext behavior otherwise. An exception created inside a translated context must still render its standard wrappers in that context's language after the context has exited. Nested contexts, independently overridden singular/plural callbacks and separate threads must stay isolated. Do not mutate process-wide gettext functions, environment locale, existing commands or shared parameter types to switch a language. Preserve exception types, exit codes, callback behavior, parameter values, command parsing and help wrapping.

Add focused regressions in the relevant existing command/help, parameter type, parser, exception, decorator, terminal UI and shell completion tests. Exercise default compatibility, translation before interpolation, plurals, callbacks supplied through context_settings, explicit-context operations outside a scope, nested inheritance and overrides, command reuse, deferred error rendering, invalid callbacks and results, and thread isolation. Document the public API and provide runnable examples using two languages and parent/child commands. Run the complete repository test suite and its available source/style checks, fixing regressions introduced by the feature. Finish with a concise implementation and verification report. Make routine implementation choices autonomously.
